templates.pattern: A cyclist travels a distance of [D] km in [T] hours. Calculate the average speed of the cyclist in km/h.
templates.explanation:
Average speed = Distance ÷ Time
= [D] ÷ [T]
= [RESULT] km/h

Always divide total distance by total time to find average speed.

templates.pattern: A train travels at a constant speed of [S] km/h for [T] hours. Calculate the total distance travelled by the train in km.
templates.explanation:
Distance = Speed × Time
= [S] × [T]
= [RESULT] km

When speed is constant, multiply speed by time to find distance.

templates.pattern: A car travels [D] km at a constant speed of [S] km/h. Calculate the time taken for the journey in hours.
templates.explanation:
Time = Distance ÷ Speed
= [D] ÷ [S]
= [RESULT] hours

Rearrange speed = distance ÷ time to get time = distance ÷ speed.

templates.pattern: A motorbike increases its velocity from [U] m/s to [V] m/s in [T] seconds. Calculate the acceleration of the motorbike in m/s².
templates.explanation:
Acceleration = (Final velocity − Initial velocity) ÷ Time
= ([V] − [U]) ÷ [T]
= [ACC*T] ÷ [T]
= [RESULT] m/s²

Acceleration is the rate of change of velocity over time.

templates.pattern: A resultant force of [F] N acts on an object of mass [M] kg. Calculate the acceleration of the object in m/s².
templates.explanation:
Using Newton's Second Law: F = m × a
Rearranging: a = F ÷ m
= [F] ÷ [M]
= [RESULT] m/s²

The greater the force or the smaller the mass, the greater the acceleration.

templates.pattern: A ball of mass [M] kg is moving at a velocity of [V] m/s. Calculate the kinetic energy of the ball in joules.
templates.explanation:
Kinetic Energy = ½ × mass × velocity²
= 0.5 × [M] × [V]²
= 0.5 × [M] × [V*V]
= [RESULT] J

Kinetic energy depends on the square of velocity — doubling speed quadruples KE.

templates.pattern: A crate of mass [M] kg is lifted vertically to a height of [H] m above the ground. Calculate the gravitational potential energy gained by the crate. (g = 10 m/s²)
templates.explanation:
Gravitational Potential Energy = mass × g × height
= [M] × 10 × [H]
= [RESULT] J

GPE increases with both mass and height. g = 10 m/s² at GCSE level.

templates.pattern: A person applies a force of [F] N to push a box across a floor for a distance of [D] m in the direction of the force. Calculate the work done by the person in joules.
templates.explanation:
Work Done = Force × Distance
= [F] × [D]
= [RESULT] J

Work is done only when a force causes movement in the direction of the force. One joule equals one newton-metre.

templates.pattern: An electric motor does [W] J of work in [T] seconds. Calculate the power output of the motor in watts.
templates.explanation:
Power = Work Done ÷ Time
= [W] ÷ [T]
= [RESULT] W

Power is the rate of doing work. 1 watt = 1 joule per second.

templates.pattern: An object has a mass of [M] kg. Calculate its weight on [PLANET] where the gravitational field strength is [G] N/kg.
templates.explanation:
Weight = mass × gravitational field strength
= [M] × [G]
= [RESULT] N

Weight changes on different planets but mass always stays the same. Mass is constant everywhere in the universe.
